tasks.short: Run practical training sessions for warehouse teams, drivers and office staff across our three sites.

today.trigger: A scheduled course, new working procedure or supervisor request calls for a training session.
steps: Check learning objectives, participants' experience and language needs.
Prepare slides, demonstrations, exercises and discussion prompts.
Arrange a room, equipment and time around shifts.
Deliver the session and adjust to questions and practical difficulties.
Check understanding and record attendance or refer participants for practical assessment.
drudgery: Rewriting the same examples for different teams.
Preparing exercise sheets and attendance records.
Repeating explanations when participants need another language or reading level.
today.time_sinks: Preparing variants and arranging sessions takes time; live explanation, practice and feedback remain substantial.

lenses.faster: Draft exercises, facilitator notes and language variants from an approved lesson outline. Attendance capture removes later retyping.
lenses.autonomous: A confirmed session can trigger preparation of a facilitator pack and participant reminders. The specialist leads delivery and responds to the group.
lenses.ambitious: Give every new warehouse starter realistic practice for common errors, followed by short refresher sessions during the first 90 days.
lenses.joy: Remove slide formatting and repetitive preparation. Keep demonstrations, lively discussion and the moment someone masters a skill.
lenses.options: Prepare five ways to teach the same procedure, including a demonstration, team exercise, scenario, visual guide and discussion.
lenses.altitude: Design reusable teaching formats and coach supervisors to deliver them consistently across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
reach: Help HR Business Partners equip supervisors to coach new starters.
Help Recruiters explain the practical skills covered during onboarding.

tasks.human_edge: The trainer notices confusion, builds trust and adapts the session. A qualified person must judge practical competence and safe equipment use.
tasks.pattern_why: AI can prepare and adapt teaching aids, but live facilitation and practical assessment depend on human presence and judgment.

in_practice.trigger: The specialist confirms a session brief with an approved procedure, audience and learning objectives.
steps: Retrieve the current approved procedure and reusable teaching templates.
Draft exercises, facilitator notes and participant materials, with references to the source.
Have the specialist check technical accuracy, language and suitability for the group.
Deliver the session with human supervision of practical activities.
Record attendance and human assessment results in Studytube through a supported import or manual entry.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves all teaching materials and leads the session; an appropriately qualified assessor signs off practical competence.
data_needed: Approved procedures and their version dates.
Learning objectives and practical assessment criteria.
Group size, job roles, site and shift.
Language and accessibility needs supplied for training purposes.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint session record containing source versions and approved materials; attendance and assessment outcomes in Studytube.

evidence.claim: A language model can draft role-play scenarios and alternative explanations from supplied procedures.
Saving 25% of specialist effort with a 1.2-fold end-to-end speedup is an untested planning estimate; live delivery remains.

risks: Generated exercises could teach an unsafe procedure or omit an important exception.
Translations may use unfamiliar warehouse terms or change the meaning of safety instructions.
Recorded completion could be mistaken for demonstrated practical competence.
Training schedules must respect applicable CAO provisions on paid training time, working hours and rest.
research_questions: How much of these 140.6 annual hours per specialist is preparation versus live delivery?
Can supervisors and safety assessors approve generated exercises with fewer corrections than current materials?
Do language variants improve demonstrated understanding across representative shift groups?
Can attendance be recorded once and transferred to Studytube without duplicate entry?

tasks.short: Turn our procedures into clear course materials, quick guides and handouts.

today.trigger: A new course, changed procedure or outdated guide requires new training materials.
steps: Collect current procedures, policies and existing course files.
Ask operational experts to resolve gaps and conflicting instructions.
Write and format guides, slides, handouts and knowledge checks.
Arrange technical review and correct the materials.
Publish approved versions and replace outdated copies.
drudgery: Copying the same procedure into several formats.
Formatting documents and rewriting standard explanations.
Finding and replacing outdated versions.
today.time_sinks: Source reconciliation, first drafts, formatting and repeated edits across different files.

lenses.faster: Generate a guide, slide outline and knowledge check from one approved source package. Template-based formatting removes repeated copying and layout work.
lenses.autonomous: An approved procedure change can trigger draft updates and a review request. Publication follows named human approval.
lenses.ambitious: Provide current visual guides for every critical warehouse procedure, with language variants and short refreshers available on each shift.
lenses.joy: Remove document assembly and version chasing. Keep instructional design and conversations with experts about what workers actually need.
lenses.options: Compare a one-page visual guide, a short course, a supervisor briefing and a practice exercise before choosing the right combination.
lenses.altitude: Own the content standards, source hierarchy and review cycle for a reusable training library.
reach: Help HR Administrators maintain onboarding guidance and policy explanations.
Help operational procedure owners turn technical instructions into usable employee guidance.

tasks.human_edge: People decide which instructions are authoritative, what learners need and whether safety guidance is correct.
tasks.pattern_why: Drafting, formatting and update tracking can run as a workflow, but conflicting sources and publication need accountable approval.

in_practice.trigger: A procedure owner approves a new source version or the specialist opens a content request.
steps: Collect approved source documents and flag contradictions or missing instructions.
Draft the requested materials using company templates and source references.
Run deterministic checks for required sections, version labels and broken links.
Send the draft and a change summary to the specialist and relevant technical owner.
After approval, publish through supported Studytube and SharePoint methods and archive superseded versions.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves learning quality; the procedure owner or safety expert approves technical content before publication.
systems: Proposed company-approved AI drafting and workflow service
data_needed: Approved procedures with owners and version history.
Company document templates and terminology.
Course objectives and intended audience.
Publication locations and review permissions.
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint content register linking source versions, generated drafts, reviewer decisions and published Studytube materials.

evidence.claim: Language models can convert supplied source text into draft guides, slide outlines and questions.
SharePoint supports document version history, which can underpin a controlled content register.
Saving 65% of specialist effort with a twofold end-to-end speedup is untested and depends on source quality and reviewer availability.

risks: An outdated source could produce polished but incorrect materials.
A knowledge check could reward memorization while missing unsafe practical behavior.
Copyright or supplier licensing may restrict adaptation of purchased course materials.
Uncontrolled publication could leave different sites using different instructions.
research_questions: What share of frequently used procedures has a clearly identified owner and approved current version?
Which Studytube authoring, import and publication functions are available under Noordhaven's contract?
How many substantive corrections do reviewers make to generated materials compared with current first drafts?
Can one approved source reliably update every published derivative without leaving obsolete copies?

tasks.short: Arrange and deliver the job training people need to work safely and improve their skills.

today.trigger: A starter, role change, certificate expiry or supervisor request creates a training need.
steps: Check the worker's role, existing training and required certificates.
Discuss gaps and suitable courses with the worker and supervisor.
Find a provider or arrange internal training around shifts.
Enroll the worker, deliver support and follow up on attendance.
Record completion and arrange practical assessment or further coaching.
drudgery: Checking certificate expiry lists.
Repeating enrollment and reminder messages.
Chasing attendance and missing evidence.
today.time_sinks: Reconciling training requirements, booking around shifts and following up with workers, supervisors and agencies.

lenses.faster: Match approved role requirements against recorded training and prepare booking options. Remove manual expiry checks and routine reminder writing.
lenses.autonomous: Joiners, role changes and upcoming expiries can trigger a training proposal and reminders. Supervisors approve release time and specialists handle exceptions.
lenses.ambitious: Give permanent and flex workers a clear skills path, including refreshers before expiry and supported practice after each course.
lenses.joy: Remove chasing and enrollment administration. Keep coaching workers and helping them progress into more skilled jobs.
lenses.options: Compare internal practice, an external course and a blended route against cost, shift coverage and demonstrated skill needs.
lenses.altitude: Manage a role-based skills and certificate system instead of assembling each worker's training from scratch.
reach: Help HR Administrators manage training steps after role changes.
Help staffing agency coordinators verify agreed training evidence for flex workers.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist and supervisor judge readiness, motivation and practical skill; a course record alone does not authorize hazardous work.
tasks.pattern_why: Rules can identify routine requirements and prepare enrollment, while course selection, shift release and competence decisions need human approval.

in_practice.trigger: An approved AFAS joiner or role-change record, a verified flex-worker intake, or a certificate approaching expiry.
steps: Apply an approved role-to-training matrix to verified worker and certificate records.
Flag missing, expired or uncertain evidence and propose suitable training.
Check available courses and obtain supervisor approval for release time and cost.
Enroll through supported methods and send approved reminders.
Record verified completion and request human practical sign-off where required.
in_practice.human_gate: A supervisor approves schedule and release time; the specialist approves exceptions and an authorized assessor confirms practical competence.
systems: Staffing agency portals or agreed exports
data_needed: Approved role-to-training requirements, including site and client requirements.
Worker identity, employment or agency status and assigned role.
Certificate evidence, expiry dates and verification status.
Course availability, costs, shift schedules and applicable CAO arrangements.
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube training records and a restricted SharePoint exception log, with flex-worker evidence shared only through agreed agency channels.

evidence.claim: Studytube holds courses, enrollments, completions and certificates in the company's stated setup.
evidence.source: Studytube; company setup supplied in the prompt

evidence.claim: A rules-based workflow can compare certificate dates with approved role requirements and prepare reminders.
Saving 30% of specialist effort with a 1.3-fold end-to-end speedup is untested; course dates and shift release remain constraints.

risks: Incorrect role mappings could omit required training or assign unnecessary courses.
Forklift, VCA and food-safety requirements must be defined for the actual work; they are not interchangeable or universally applicable.
Flex-worker records may be incomplete, duplicated or outside the company's licensed LMS access.
Automated training recommendations must not become unchecked decisions about promotion, work allocation or employee capability.
research_questions: Can operational owners agree and maintain a complete role-to-training matrix?
How often are certificate records missing or unreliable, particularly for flex workers?
Do available interfaces support enrollment and reminders without duplicate records?
Would administration savings matter if course capacity and shift release remain the main delays?

tasks.short: Track training completion and check whether it helps starters become productive and stay beyond 90 days.

today.trigger: A weekly review, completed course or manager question requires training records or an effectiveness assessment.
steps: Export training attendance, completion and certificate records.
Reconcile worker identities and missing records against AFAS.
Collect learner feedback and supervisor observations.
Compare results by course, site and cohort with onboarding and 90-day outcomes.
Discuss findings, agree changes and update reports.
drudgery: Combining exports and resolving duplicate worker records.
Chasing feedback and missing completions.
Writing the same report commentary each month.
today.time_sinks: Data cleaning and report assembly leave limited time to test whether training changes behavior.

lenses.faster: Use maintained data joins and fixed metric definitions to produce completion and cohort reports. AI can summarize approved feedback and draft commentary for review.
lenses.autonomous: Scheduled extracts can refresh routine metrics and create a queue of missing or inconsistent records. People investigate exceptions and interpret effectiveness.
lenses.ambitious: Evaluate each major onboarding course against week-one completion, time to demonstrated competence and 90-day retention, with comparable cohorts.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet reconciliation and repetitive reporting. Keep finding out why a course works and improving it with supervisors.
lenses.options: Compare outcomes by site, shift and delivery method, showing uncertainty and differences in participant mix.
lenses.altitude: Own the learning measurement system and the experiments that improve hire-to-productive results.
reach: Take on first-line training data checks for the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
Help HR Business Partners investigate onboarding failures using cohort evidence.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist distinguishes genuine learning effects from staffing, supervisor, site and recruitment differences.
tasks.pattern_why: Record joins, date checks and metric calculations are checkable software tasks. Optional feedback summaries use an LLM step, while interpretation stays human.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled data refresh or a completed training cohort.
steps: Load approved AFAS and Studytube extracts and validate identity matches, dates and completeness.
Calculate agreed completion, certificate and onboarding cohort metrics with deterministic code.
Flag data exceptions and suppress small groups that could expose individuals.
Prepare a source-linked summary of aggregated feedback and observed outcome differences.
Have the specialist review interpretations and agree course changes with operational owners.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine validated metrics refresh without individual approval; effectiveness claims and proposed interventions require specialist review.
data_needed: Stable worker identifiers, start dates, sites and roles.
Enrollment, attendance, completion and assessment dates.
Agreed definitions of productive status and 90-day retention.
Supervisor observations and learner feedback.
Data access rules, suppression thresholds and extract timestamps.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI refresh and validation records, plus a restricted SharePoint register of evaluation decisions and source-linked summaries.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports data transformation, relationships and scheduled reporting.
Cohort comparisons can inform training evaluation but do not establish that training caused retention or productivity differences.
Saving 55% of specialist effort with a 1.8-fold end-to-end speedup is untested and depends on reliable identity matching and outcome records.

risks: Completion may be reported as competence without a practical assessment.
Site, shift and manager differences could be mistaken for a training effect.
Small cohorts or free-text feedback may identify individual workers under AVG/GDPR.
The nightly AFAS extract is too stale for real-time decisions about permission to perform safety-critical work.
research_questions: Is productive status measured consistently by supervisors, with a date and clear assessment criteria?
Can Studytube and AFAS records be matched reliably for permanent and flex workers?
Are cohorts large and comparable enough to support useful outcome analysis?
How much reporting time remains after data cleaning and calculations are automated?

tasks.short: Build and coordinate onboarding and training plans that fit each job, site and shift.

today.trigger: A confirmed starter, seasonal intake or operational change requires an orientation or training program.
steps: Confirm roles, start dates, site needs and supervisor expectations.
Design the sequence of orientation, mandatory learning and practical training.
Arrange trainers, buddies, rooms and shift release.
Send plans and enrollment instructions to workers and managers.
Track week-one progress and adjust support through day 90.
drudgery: Copying standard onboarding plans for each starter.
Repeated calendar coordination and reminders.
Chasing missing ownership and handoffs.
today.time_sinks: Reconstructing starter information and coordinating many dependencies across sites, shifts and agencies.

lenses.faster: Generate a draft onboarding plan from approved role, site and shift templates. Prepare bookings and named responsibilities in one place.
lenses.autonomous: An approved AFAS starter record or verified agency intake can launch the standard workflow. Late starts, missing buddies and conflicting schedules go to an exception queue.
lenses.ambitious: Provide every starter with a coordinated day-one, week-one and day-90 path, including flex workers during seasonal peaks.
lenses.joy: Remove copy-paste plans and handoff chasing. Keep designing a welcoming start and solving problems that put retention at risk.
lenses.options: Compare staggered starts, group induction and shift-based induction against trainer capacity, coverage and week-one completion.
lenses.altitude: Own the onboarding service and improve the handoffs between recruiting, HR administration, supervisors and agencies.
reach: Coordinate the Recruiter's accepted-offer handoff into onboarding.
Take on routine onboarding coordination from HR Administrators and HR Business Partners.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist designs a realistic learning journey; supervisors commit time, choose suitable buddies and support people whose first weeks are difficult.
tasks.pattern_why: Several systems and scheduling dependencies can be coordinated automatically, but the initial plan needs supervisor approval and exceptions need human decisions.

in_practice.trigger: An approved starter record reaches the agreed onboarding lead time, or an agency intake is verified.
steps: Read the minimum starter details and select the approved role, site and shift template.
Build a proposed learning sequence with prerequisites, deadlines and named owners.
Check trainer, buddy and shift availability and flag unresolved conflicts.
Obtain supervisor and specialist approval, then create supported enrollments and calendar invitations.
Track agreed milestones, send routine reminders and route missed or blocked steps to the responsible person.
in_practice.human_gate: The supervisor approves release time, buddy and practical sequence; the specialist approves the initial plan and material deviations.
systems: Recruitee for an agreed minimal accepted-offer handoff
Staffing agency portals or agreed intake files
data_needed: Verified start date, role, site, shift and supervisor.
Approved onboarding templates and prerequisite rules.
Trainer, buddy and room availability.
Agency responsibilities and permitted flex-worker data.
Week-one and day-90 milestone definitions.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint onboarding register with approvals and exceptions; course progress in Studytube and authoritative employment details in AFAS.

evidence.claim: Outlook supports calendar invitations and shared scheduling, while Studytube holds enrollments in the stated company setup.
Template selection, milestone tracking and reminder routing can be implemented as a rules-based workflow.
Saving 45% of specialist effort with a 1.5-fold end-to-end speedup is untested; trainer and supervisor capacity still determine many dates.

risks: Changed start dates or no-shows could create unnecessary bookings and enrollments.
A complete checklist could conceal a poor welcome or weak practical support.
Sharing Recruitee interview feedback would exceed the data needed for routine onboarding.
Changes to company training arrangements may require OR consent under the WOR; confirm the scope before introducing a new policy.
research_questions: Which onboarding delays arise from administration, and which arise from unavailable trainers or supervisors?
Are starter dates and agency intakes reliable early enough to trigger planning?
Can existing templates specify accountable owners for every week-one milestone?
Does a pilot improve week-one completion and supervisor satisfaction without increasing interruptions on shifts?

tasks.short: Choose training formats that teach the skill well and fit our shifts, costs and travel needs.

today.trigger: A course renewal, new program or disappointing result prompts a review of delivery methods.
steps: Gather prices, course duration, attendance and learner feedback.
Estimate paid training time, travel, backfill and equipment needs.
Compare classroom, virtual, practical and blended approaches.
Discuss suitability and constraints with supervisors and safety experts.
Recommend a format and review results after a pilot.
drudgery: Rebuilding cost comparison spreadsheets.
Normalizing provider offers with different inclusions.
Summarizing the same feedback by hand.
today.time_sinks: Collecting comparable inputs and estimating the full cost of shift release and travel.

lenses.faster: Extract comparable fields from provider offers, then calculate costs with a fixed spreadsheet model. Draft the comparison from checked numbers and feedback.
lenses.autonomous: A review date can refresh available inputs and flag missing quotes. The specialist still chooses the learning criteria and recommends a delivery method.
lenses.ambitious: Test alternative formats for major courses and measure demonstrated skill, access across shifts, cost and travel impact before wider rollout.
lenses.joy: Remove quote transcription and repeated calculations. Keep designing pilots and discussing what actually helps workers learn.
lenses.options: Compare five delivery scenarios, including local practical groups, central classroom sessions, live virtual teaching, self-paced learning and a blended route.
lenses.altitude: Set standards for choosing and testing delivery methods across the training portfolio.
reach: Prepare training business-case inputs for FP&A.
Help procurement and operational managers compare training-provider offers.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides whether a method suits the skill and the workers; safety experts decide which practical elements cannot be replaced.
tasks.pattern_why: Software can calculate scenarios and AI can normalize quotes, but selecting delivery methods requires learning judgment and consultation.

in_practice.trigger: A course enters its review window or an operational owner requests a new delivery approach.
steps: Collect provider offers, existing outcomes and shift-access constraints.
Extract quote details into a common schema and have the specialist verify ambiguous terms.
Calculate total cost and travel estimates using approved formulas and explicit assumptions.
Generate delivery scenarios with separate measures for learning, access, cost and environmental impact.
Have the specialist recommend a pilot and agree evaluation criteria with operational owners.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist verifies quote interpretation and learning suitability; budget and operational owners approve the pilot and spend.
data_needed: Provider prices, inclusions, cancellation terms and course duration.
Paid training-time rules and approved labor-cost assumptions.
Shift release, backfill, travel and equipment requirements.
Completion, practical assessment and feedback data.
Explicit travel-emissions factors if environmental comparisons are required.
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint decision file containing verified inputs, scenario calculations, assumptions, approvals and pilot results.

evidence.claim: Excel can calculate auditable delivery-cost scenarios using fixed formulas and explicit assumptions.
Language models can extract comparison fields from quotes, with human checks for ambiguous exclusions and terms.
Saving 40% of specialist effort with a 1.4-fold end-to-end speedup is untested and depends on quote quality and consultation time.

risks: A cheap online option may fail to teach or assess a practical safety skill.
Uncounted backfill, allowances or overtime could reverse the apparent saving.
Travel-emissions estimates may imply precision unsupported by the available data.
Workers may lack devices, quiet study space or paid access time on shifts.
research_questions: Do current comparisons include paid learning time, backfill and applicable CAO costs?
Which courses have practical assessment results suitable for comparing delivery methods?
Can quote extraction capture exclusions and cancellation terms accurately enough to reduce review effort?
Can workers on every shift access the proposed format without using personal time or equipment?

tasks.short: Keep our training approach current by reading relevant research, sector updates and Dutch guidance.

today.trigger: A weekly reading slot, sector update or unfamiliar training problem prompts research.
steps: Search trusted publications, sector sources and official guidance.
Read relevant articles and check publication dates and context.
Compare findings with Noordhaven's current training approach.
Save useful sources and share implications with colleagues.
Select ideas to test or changes that need expert review.
drudgery: Searching several sources for the same topic.
Reading duplicate announcements and promotional articles.
Writing summaries and maintaining reading notes.
today.time_sinks: Filtering weak material, locating original evidence and deciding whether findings apply to shift-based logistics work.

lenses.faster: Prepare a source-linked digest from selected publications and approved subscriptions. Remove duplicate stories and highlight passages relevant to current training questions.
lenses.autonomous: A weekly schedule can collect accessible updates and draft a reading queue. The specialist reads original sources before acting on important claims.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a small evidence library for shift learning, multilingual instruction, practical assessment and onboarding retention, with one useful pilot each quarter.
lenses.joy: Remove search noise and summary writing. Keep learning, questioning assumptions and discussing promising ideas.
lenses.options: For a training problem, compare several approaches and include evidence that challenges the preferred solution.
lenses.altitude: Run an evidence-to-practice process that turns selected findings into measured improvements.
reach: Brief HR Business Partners on learning and onboarding evidence.
Help the HR Director identify training implications of sector and regulatory changes.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist assesses evidence quality and local relevance, and seeks qualified advice on legal or safety implications.
tasks.pattern_why: The useful AI step is turning retrieved text into a structured, source-linked digest inside a scheduled collection workflow.

in_practice.trigger: A weekly digest schedule or a research question entered by the specialist.
steps: Collect accessible material from an approved source list and respect subscription restrictions.
Deduplicate items and retain title, author, publication date and original link.
Summarize relevant passages and separate findings, limitations and suggested applications.
Have the specialist inspect originals for shortlisted or consequential claims.
Record a decision to ignore, monitor, seek expert advice or run a measured pilot.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist verifies shortlisted claims against originals before sharing recommendations; legal and safety changes go to the appropriate expert.
data_needed: Approved publications and permitted subscription access.
Current research questions and company learning priorities.
Source text, publication dates and original links.
Existing training practices and earlier pilot results.
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint evidence library with original links, dated summaries, verification notes and decisions.

evidence.claim: Language models can summarize supplied articles and organize them into a structured digest.
Summaries need verification because a model can omit limitations or invent unsupported details.
Saving 45% of specialist effort with a 1.6-fold end-to-end speedup is untested; source verification and deeper reading remain.

risks: A summary may exaggerate a finding or omit evidence that contradicts it.
Outdated Dutch guidance may be presented as current.
Subscription terms may prohibit automated retrieval or uploading full articles to an external service.
Commercial claims may crowd out independent evidence.
research_questions: Which sources consistently change useful decisions, and which mainly create reading volume?
Can the collector access those sources lawfully and retain reliable dates and links?
Does a specialist audit find all important limitations accurately represented in the digest?
Does the digest reduce reading effort while preserving useful discoveries outside current priorities?

tasks.short: Check instructors' course materials for accuracy, clarity and fit with our warehouse and transport work.

today.trigger: An instructor submits new or revised materials before a course is approved or renewed.
steps: Read the outline, slides, handouts and assessments.
Compare the content with learning objectives and current company procedures.
Check language, examples, accessibility and coverage of required topics.
Ask the instructor or technical expert about gaps and questionable claims.
Approve the materials or request changes and review the revised version.
drudgery: Checking the same required sections in every submission.
Finding inconsistencies across slides and handouts.
Repeating standard review comments.
today.time_sinks: Detailed first-pass reading, cross-referencing procedures and rechecking revisions.

lenses.faster: Produce a source-linked first-pass review against a fixed rubric. Remove repeated coverage checks and focus human attention on disputed or safety-critical points.
lenses.autonomous: A submitted material package can trigger checks and a draft review report. Acceptance requires a named reviewer.
lenses.ambitious: Review every course consistently for procedural accuracy, language access and useful practical assessment, including revisions from external providers.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive proofreading and checklist work. Keep constructive conversations that improve teaching.
lenses.options: Suggest several repairs for a weak section, such as a clearer explanation, visual example, practice activity or better assessment question.
lenses.altitude: Own the quality rubric, approved reference set and reviewer calibration process.
reach: Provide structured course-quality evidence for procurement decisions.
Help safety and operational owners identify training content affected by procedure changes.

tasks.human_edge: A reviewer judges educational suitability and resolves ambiguous claims; a technical expert remains accountable for safety accuracy.
tasks.pattern_why: Most first-pass checks and the review report can be produced automatically, but course acceptance and technical safety approval require human decisions.

in_practice.trigger: An instructor uploads a complete submission to the designated SharePoint review folder.
steps: Check required files, readable content, version labels and course objectives.
Compare materials with the approved rubric and reference documents.
Create findings with page or slide references, source citations and suggested corrections.
Have the specialist and relevant technical expert resolve consequential findings and approve or return the package.
Recheck revisions and record the final approved version before publication.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist accepts learning quality and the technical owner signs off safety-critical content; an automated score cannot approve a course.
data_needed: Instructor materials and course objectives.
Approved procedures and required topic lists.
Review rubric, accessibility requirements and terminology.
Previous review findings and final approval decisions.
Permissions to process externally supplied materials.
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint review register containing submission versions, source-linked findings, reviewer dispositions and final approval.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft rubric-based document reviews with references to supplied text.
Deterministic checks can verify required sections, file presence and version labels.
Saving 55% of specialist effort with a 1.7-fold end-to-end speedup is untested; instructor revisions and technical review remain dependencies.

risks: The review may miss an unsafe instruction or falsely flag a valid one.
Text extraction may omit important diagrams, demonstrations or speaker notes.
A rubric may reward tidy documents while missing poor teaching or weak assessment.
Provider confidentiality and copyright terms may restrict external AI processing.
research_questions: On previously reviewed materials, does the workflow detect known consequential defects without excessive false alarms?
Can it inspect diagrams, slide notes and scanned handouts sufficiently for the courses in scope?
Do source-linked findings reduce specialist review time after verification is included?
Can reviewers agree on the rubric and consistently resolve disputed findings?

role.altitude: The Learning and Development Specialist becomes the owner of Noordhaven's learning and onboarding system: approved content, role requirements, practical assessment, delivery standards and evidence of effectiveness.
reach: Routine onboarding coordination currently handled by HR Administrators and Recruiters.
Training data validation and cohort reporting support for the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
Supervisor coaching and onboarding improvement work with HR Business Partners.
Training cost scenarios and provider comparisons for FP&A and procurement.
Coordination of flex-worker training evidence with staffing agencies and operational supervisors.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks cover about 53% of the role: 850.1 hours per FTE annually. The proposed effort reductions total about 374 hours per FTE, or 748 hours across two FTE, roughly 23% of their assumed 3,200 annual working hours and EUR 50,900 of capacity at EUR 68/hour. These are untested estimates, not cash savings; shared workflow benefits must be counted once, and setup, maintenance and adoption effort reduce the net benefit. Speedups estimate elapsed task time, while time_saved_pct estimates specialist effort. Live facilitation, practical assessment, expert approval, shift release and course capacity limit further gains.
skills_to_grow: Designing role-based training requirements and practical assessment criteria.
Maintaining approved source documents, reusable templates and review rubrics.
Specifying workflows, exceptions and acceptance checks with the HRIS Analyst.
Evaluating cohort outcomes without confusing correlation with causation.
Designing accessible learning for different languages, literacy levels and shifts.
Applying CAO training-time provisions and involving the OR where training arrangements require consent.
Using AVG/GDPR data minimization, access controls and retention rules; keeping medical and Wet verbetering poortwachter case information with authorized absence professionals.
Recognizing when AI-based worker assessment or vocational-training decisions could fall under EU AI Act high-risk rules and obtaining a use-specific assessment.
role.ambitious_version: Give every permanent and flex starter a clear route from day one to demonstrated competence and a successful day 90. Use current multilingual materials, reliable certificate records and supervisor-led practical coaching across all three sites, then test which learning changes improve productivity and retention. Spend released capacity on better learning and manager support, with proportionate records rather than intrusive individual monitoring.
